title: Welcome to the 3D Web
description: 3D graphics on the web have evolved from simple experiments to high-performance, immersive experiences. We'll journey from fundamental geometry to professional React-based staging using Three.js and React Three Fiber.

title: Vertices: The Atomic Unit
description: Everything in 3D starts with a Point or 'Vertex'. A vertex defines a position in 3D space using X (width), Y (height), and Z (depth) coordinates. They are the scaffolding for all complex shapes.

title: Edges: Creating Structure
description: When we connect two vertices, we create an Edge. These lines form the 'wireframe' of an object, defining its skeleton and topological flow before any surfaces are added.

title: Faces: Defining Surfaces
description: Three or more connected vertices form a Face (usually a triangle in WebGL). Faces are what make an object 'solid', allowing the GPU to calculate how light hits a surface and how textures are projected.

title: The Vanilla Engine
description: Understanding the core 'Three.js' engine is vital. It requires manual setup of the Scene (world), Camera (eyes), and Renderer (painter), alongside a recursive Animation Loop to keep the frame updating.

title: R3F: Declarative 3D
description: React Three Fiber (R3F) transforms Three.js into a declarative React environment. Instead of manual scene management, you use components. State (like adding boxes) is handled just like a standard web app.

title: Lighting & Navigation
description: A 3D scene is 'flat' without lighting. AmbientLight provides base illumination, while DirectionalLight creates depth. 'OrbitControls' from the Drei library enables intuitive camera navigation.

title: Geometries & Math
description: Three.js provides many primitive geometries out of the box. In R3F, we pass constructor arguments via the 'args' prop. High segment counts lead to smoother curves but require more GPU power.

title: Materials & Physicality
description: Materials define how a light reacts to a surface. MeshStandardMaterial uses PBR (Physically Based Rendering) for realism. Textures can be mapped to simulate complex details without adding geometry.

title: The Native Render Loop
description: Animation in R3F happens within the 'useFrame' hook. This hook gives you access to the internal render loop, allowing for frame-by-frame updates that are much more efficient than using standard React state for motion.

title: Interaction & Events
description: Interactivity is built directly into R3F. Meshes support familiar events like onClick, onPointerEnter, and onPointerLeave. R3F handles the heavy lifting of 'Raycasting' behind the scenes.

title: Professional Staging
description: Production scenes combine many advanced features. Photorealistic lighting often uses 'Environment' presets, while textures are mapped to simulate complex details without adding geometry. In R3F, we use the 'useTexture' hook to load and apply these maps.
